decision: Analyzed StS1 comprehensively via 4 parallel research delegates, then scoped to the map layer
why: needed the real mechanics before deciding what to emulate; the gap report showed structure is specced but zero of it is implemented

decision: Will NOT build HP, block, potions, buffs, or damage math
why: HP has no honest analogue in project work, so a health bar would be decorative theater and the repo non-goals already forbid mandatory gamification

decision: Chose the seeded map generator as the first unit
why: it is the foundational data structure everything else hangs off, it is pure stdlib, and it is the one load-bearing StS pillar that is fully implementable and fully checkable

decision: Wrote the invariant tests before the generator and committed them red
why: so the stack reads as an argument: the rules are real before any code claims to satisfy them

decision: Implemented the generator; 28 of 31 tests passed first run
why: faithful port of the documented algorithm rather than an invented one

decision: Exempted forced floors from the parent and sibling rules instead of changing the generator
why: the invariant was over-broad, not the code. StS forces an all-treasure and an all-rest floor, so siblings there necessarily share a kind

decision: Fixed inverted diagonal glyphs in the ASCII renderer
why: caught by reading the rendered map rather than trusting green tests

decision: Shipped mapgen.py verify as the rerunnable invariant check
why: a reviewer can rerun one command instead of redoing the analysis

decision: Generated map data from Python instead of porting the generator to JS
why: one implementation of the rules; the demo renders what the engine produced

decision: Browser test caught that Enter node threw on every click
why: the generated data was missing the rolls array the client needs to resolve unknown nodes

decision: Rebased this branch onto the demo branch rather than main
why: the map work is only visible on top of the demo, so stacking is the honest delivery order

decision: Climbed 6 floors in the browser using Enter node every time
why: the predicate was routing a real branching map end to end, not just green tests

decision: Added a test that fails when mapdata.js drifts from the generator
why: the same mistake would otherwise ship silently, since the demo reads a committed generated file

decision: Full predicate check on the real artifacts
why: purity, every placement invariant, frozen unknowns, edge-legal traversal, lint and tests, and a routable demo

decision: Supersedes the red-tests row: its commit c1a0db9 was orphaned when I rebased onto the demo branch
why: the SHA no longer appears in the delivered history, so the pointer was misleading to a reviewer

decision: Supersedes the generator row: its commit 6d505d4 was orphaned by the same rebase
why: same cause; recording it rather than quietly repointing the original row

decision: Supersedes the HP-refusal row's evidence pointer
why: non-goals.md supports the reason but the decision itself lives in the ledger

decision: Cross-model review found three real bugs; reproduced all three before touching code
why: the reviewer could have been wrong, and two of them contradicted claims already in the PR body
evidence: measured 600/600 monster corridors, 54% rejoin violations, no boss in KINDS

decision: Assign bag items to random legal slots instead of dealing row by row
why: row-major dealing let the bottom floors drain every shop and unknown before the top was reached

decision: Retry a path walk that would add a rejoin, rather than only preferring not to
why: edge surgery afterwards plateaued at 54% clean; fixing it at the source reached 100%

decision: Added the boss as a real node and inverted the invariant that forbade it
why: the checker was enforcing the opposite of the spec, which is why the dead act advance passed

decision: Export the ramp config from Python instead of restating it in JS
why: the parity test compared Python to Python, so it could not have caught client drift

decision: Settled the entity mapping on one rule: how a thing is spent, not what it is
why: it decides the cases people argue about, so a linter is a relic and a profiler run is a potion

decision: Added Deck and Metrics facets; silhouette carries meaning so objects survive greyscale
why: the user asked to see the codebase as a run, and colour alone fails colour-blind readers

decision: Acts are unbounded; beating the Heart continues the climb
why: a codebase does not finish, so a terminus would be the dishonest part

decision: Reported combat bug was a dead control, not broken state
why: illegal cards were disabled and gave no feedback; the logic was fine but the UI lied

decision: Added a boot content audit for room clearability
why: the endless boss shipped unclearable because nothing checked that a room type had legal cards

decision: Used runtime instrumentation after two wrong guesses about the dead map clicks
why: I had already guessed twice; the logs showed the legal nodes were rendering below the fold and Chrome swallows clicks on disabled buttons

decision: Rotated the map to horizontal instead of restoring the inner scroller
why: formats/map.md always specified left to boss, and it removes the off-screen class of bug rather than patching it

decision: Refreshed the evidence artifact; the earlier one was captured before the last commit
why: the previous review caught it claiming 153 tests when the PR said 156

decision: Ran the cross-model review on cursor-grok-4.5-high after the user named the model
why: the skill requires a different model family and the earlier default slugs were unavailable here

decision: Supersedes row 9: it cited verify --seeds 400 producing 2400 maps
why: the CLI has since grown acts and ascensions, so that arithmetic no longer holds; 2400 is 200 seeds x 6 acts x 2 ascensions

decision: Hashed the per-act seed instead of adding an offset
why: reviewer found seed 199 act 1 and seed 0 act 2 produced identical graphs

decision: Corrected two sections of sts-fidelity.md that described code we do not run
why: a reference doc that lies is worse than no doc, because reviewers verify against it

decision: Split the HP and potion ledger rows rather than defending the demo
why: the demo shipped a progress meter and a potions panel under rows that said refuse, which read as a contradiction and fairly so

decision: Added quota and branch-point invariants; check_invariants no longer raises
why: I had claimed quota coverage that did not exist, and the checker crashed on malformed input instead of reporting

decision: Kept the narrow rejoin rule instead of implementing the three-row version
why: a backtracking walker is not worth it for a texture rule; the doc now says so instead of overclaiming

decision: Pre-ship review found generate() returning maps that fail its own checker
why: my 200-seed sweep called them legal, which is how a 1-in-12000 defect reached a PR claiming every invariant holds
evidence: seeds (2520,5) and (1631,4), now pinned as tests

decision: Fixed the inverted active-room banner and added a real room lock
why: a reviewer entered combat then bought from the shop, which is the no-multi-room-multitasking refusal broken in the shipped demo
result: nav disabled, map refuses, verified in browser

decision: Cleared 8 mypy errors and 4 contrast failures
why: CLAUDE.md requires a clean type checker and the design system requires AA; both were being claimed without being met

decision: Retargeted PR 10 from the demo branch to main
why: the user asked for every branch to ship into main; PR 10 contains PR 9 so merging it alone lands both

decision: Left all PRs at their current draft state
why: marking ready for review is a merge-state change and was not asked for
